title: Void vs voidable marriage - a distinction every client should understand
p1:
Not every marriage that has a legal problem is treated the same way.

Many people assume that if a marriage is invalid, it simply disappears. But the law makes a crucial distinction between a void marriage and a voidable marriage.
p2:
A void marriage is considered invalid from the very beginning, as if the marriage was never legally created. A voidable marriage, however, is valid unless a court declares it invalid after one party challenges it.

The surprising part? A couple may be living together in a voidable marriage for years without the marriage being automatically cancelled.
p3:
In simple terms: void means the law treats the marriage as having no legal existence, while voidable means the marriage exists until it is legally set aside.

This difference can affect rights, legal procedures, and the steps a person must take when seeking relief. Knowing which category applies can prevent costly misunderstandings.
conclusion: Before assuming a marriage is legally invalid, would you check whether it is void or only voidable?
